World.title: Sweden: One killed in school sword attack
World.content:
Police have said they have arrested an individual who stabbed several people, killing one person, with a sword at a high school in central Sweden.

A person armed with a sword has wounded multiple people at a school in Fagersta in central Sweden, authorities said Friday.

Police said one person had been taken into custody and there was no longer any danger to the public.

After initially saying three people had been wounded in the attack, two of them severely, police later said an additional person had been killed.

Earlier on Friday, Sweden's healthcare authority said two boys, both aged between 12 and 17, were being treated in hospital.

Police said the suspect was an 18-year-old man, whom they shot during a confrontation and took into custody.

What else do we know?

Police were called to the Brinellskola, a secondary school in Fagersta, at around 2 p.m. local time (1200 GMT). The school, which has some 450 students aged 16 to 20, had just reopened after the summer holidays.

Public broadcaster SVT reported that ambulances, police cars and a police helicopter were outside the property.

The municipality said other schools and some public buildings in the area had been locked down.

Fagersta, home to some 12,000 people, lies around 170 kilometers (105 miles) northwest of the capital, Stockholm.

Police locked down other schools in the area following the attack Image: Niklas Hagman/TT/picture alliance

Reactions to 'terrible news'

"Our thoughts are with all those affected," Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said in a post on X. "We do not yet know what lies behind the act, but we know that the police are working very intensively."

Magdalena Andersson, leader of the opposition Social Democrats, lamented the "terrible news."

"When violence takes place at a school, I know it impacts everyone in our country. All of Sweden ⁠stands together with Fagersta at this difficult time," she wrote on X.

Other attacks at educational institutions

Sweden has seen a number of high-profile attacks at educational facilities in recent years.

In February 2025, a 35-year-old man killed 10 people at an adult education center in Orebro.

In another incident, an 18-year-old student fatally stabbed two teachers at a Malmo high school in March 2022.

World.title: 'Masha and the Bear': Ukraine sanctions Russian cartoon
World.content:
Ukraine has imposed sanctions on the hit Russian children's cartoon "Masha and the Bear," a step towards banning it. The culture minister called the show propaganda. Russia said the move showed Kyiv's "ugly nature."

Ukrainian Culture Minister Tetyana Berezhna on Friday said Kyiv had imposed sanctions on the "producers and distributors" of the Russian children's cartoon series "Masha and the Bear," or "Masha i Medved" in the original language.

The step will enable Kyiv to seek to remove and demonentize the series on websites like YouTube or streaming services like Netflix in the country.

The cartoon about a mischievous young girl's unlikely friendship and adventures with a retired circus bear, loosely based on a Russian oral fairytale of the same name, launched in 2009 and quickly became one of Russia's most successful televisual exports.

Masha and the Bear or Masha i Medved's YouTube channel is among the 50 most-watched in the world, with more than 54 billion views worldwide as of June 2026 Image: Ivan Sekretarev/AP Photo/picture alliance

What did the government in Kyiv say about the sanctions?

"Ukraine has imposed sanctions against the producers and distributors of the Russian animated series Masha and the Bear," Berezhna said on social media. "This creates legal grounds to block the content in Ukraine and engage international platforms to restrict its monetization and distribution."

The show has also faced criticism from allies of Ukraine like Estonia and the UK for allegedly painting Russia in a positive light or for military or Soviet symbols sometimes appearing in the show.

"Russian propaganda has no place on children's screens — in Ukraine or anywhere in the world," Berezhna said.

In further comments on Facebook, Berezhna said the Ukrainian language channel for the show had 800 million views in 2025 alone. The Ukrainian language channel currently has roughly 18 million subscribers.

Worldwide, as of June 2026, the show had more than 54 billion combined views on YouTube, making it one of the 50 most popular feeds on the entire site.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a decree imposing sanctions on the creators of the show for spreading "pro-Russia narratives" and for posing a threat to Ukrainian national security. They target the studio, the show's founder, and the series' scriptwriter and director.

Ukraine said it would seek to have its sanctions mirrored by international partners, potentially widening the restrictions.

The story revolves around a curious and sometimes mischievous girl's unlikely friendship with a protective former circus bear Image: Ivan Sekretarev/AP Photo/picture alliance

How did the show's makers and the Russian government respond?

The company behind the show, Animaccord Animation Studios, has called past allegations that the show contains Russian propaganda "false and defamatory," saying that it operates independently and receives no funding from the government in Moscow.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was asked about the sanctions on Friday and said that the cartoon series had "conquered the world" by promoting "the finest human qualities."

"The fact that Ukraine has launched a war against cartoons, too, likely serves as yet another illustration of the ugly nature" of the authorities in Kyiv, he said.

The show has a following across much of Europe — in this case as demonstrated in hay-bale form in Croatia — and even further afield Image: Davor Javorovic/PIXSELL/picture alliance

Is 'Masha and the Bear' controversial, and why?

The show has been on the radar of Ukrainian authorities for almost a decade. The first complaint by the State Film Agency dates back to 2017, amid the illegal annexation of Crimea and the lower-level war in Ukraine waged by separatists supported by Russia. Since the 2022 full-scale invasion the issue has come into sharper focus still.

In June, Kyiv protested against streaming giant Netflix's move to acquire the rights to stream new seasons of "Masha and the Bear."

A group of more than 50 British parliamentarians this year appealed to Culture Minister Lisa Nandy to urge streaming platforms to remove the cartoon. They argued that some episodes exposed children to Russian and Soviet military imagery.

Several Estonian politicians have also argued that "Masha and the Bear" is an instrument of Russian soft power, not least because of the several amiable bears in its cast.

Some Western analysts have warned against exaggerating these fears, though — for instance UK academic Mark Galeotti, who wrote an article objecting to the British lawmakers' appeal in July, saying the show was not "the most elevated of television," but "it is cute and it has a big heart."

In its earlier days, "Masha i Medved" was also a topic of some controversy in Russia. It sometimes drew critical comparisons to Western children's shows and prompted debate on whether it was contradicting traditional values about the roles of girls and fathers in Russian society, given Masha's mischievous nature and her paternal bear's gentle use of positive reinforcement rather than correctional discipline.

World.title: German army helps Poland construct a defensive barrier against Russia
World.content:
Poland is building a defense system along its northern and eastern borders to protect itself from Russia. Since June, German sappers have been assisting their NATO ally with the construction of the East Shield.

Poland started to construct a defensive barrier along its border with Russia and Belarus in 2024. The East Shield defense system will eventually be around 800 kilometers long, and is intended to protect this country on NATO's eastern flank against attack from the east.

When the Polish prime minister, Donald Tusk, inspected the first completed section in November 2024, he declared that the project was meant to "deter and discourage a potential aggressor" and was "truly an investment in peace."

The Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 was a profound shock to Poland's sense of security. The Tusk government has increased defense spending in 2026 to 200 billion zlotys (around 46 billion euros, or 54 billion dollars) ― almost 5% of Poland's GDP. This means that, in relative terms, Poland has the highest defense spending of all the members of NATO. The government has also bought the most advanced weapons available, particularly from the US, and is proceeding with the construction of the East Shield, a complex defense system along its eastern border.

A shield against Russia

Since June, around 40 German sappers, or combat engineers, have been helping to establish the defenses. The German army's combat engineer unit is specially trained in blocking the movement of enemy troops. The sappers are currently deployed near Budry in Masuria, close to the border with Russia. The fence marking the border is visible from where they are working, partially obscured by a row of trees on the Polish side.

The German soldiers are installing anti-tank obstacles to impede battle tanks in the event of an attack. A yellow backhoe loader lifts the spiky concrete blocks, known as Czech hedgehogs, off a truck and places them on the muddy ground.

This installation, around 200 meters back from the border, consists of three rows of these concrete blocks. A deep ditch and another line of hedgehogs run along the border itself. A Polish officer explains that mines can quickly be laid in the zone between the two lines of Czech hedgehogs.

"The German sappers have done an excellent job," the Polish general Stanislaw Czosnek said when he inspected the works on Thursday. He added that he was "very impressed" by his German colleagues' performance.

In the six weeks since their deployment, the German engineers have laid more than a kilometer of blocks.

"We stand ready to fight for democracy and freedom," stressed the German general Tito Gante, who accompanied Czosnek on the inspection. He praised the comradely atmosphere between the German and the Polish soldiers.

The Bundeswehr has declared its support for the East Shield an official mission: "We want to maintain peace with a credible deterrent," Gante said.

The German contingent will stay until October, but the sappers will soon be deployed at other sections of the East Shield. The work near Budry is due to be completed over the coming week.

The anti-tank obstacles can only be moved by a backhoe loader Image: Jacek Lepiarz/DW

Politically symbolic

"Above all, the participation of German sappers has politically symbolic significance," Lukasz Jasinski, an analyst at the Polish Institute for International Affairs, told DW. "Poland wants to convince Germany and other partners that Poland's eastern border is also the external border of the EU and NATO. Our Western partners should treat this border a bit like their own."

Poland and Germany were quick to establish military cooperation after the end of the Cold War. Later, when Poland joined NATO in 1999, this created the necessary political and institutional conditions for close collaboration. Since then, NATO's Multinational Corps Northeast , in which Poland and Germany both have leading roles, has been headquartered in the Polish city of Szczecin.

In 2003, Germany sold the MiG-29 fighter jets it inherited from the former East German Air Force to Poland for the symbolic price of one euro each. Joint military exercises and exchange programs for both officers and soldiers are now standard practice.

When Russia attacked Ukraine in February 2022, there were initial tensions between Germany and Poland on account of the cautious response from Berlin. Overall, though, the attack has further strengthened cooperation between the two. The Bundeswehr has supported Polish air defense by supplying several units of the Patriot air defense system, with their German crews. German fighter jets are helping to protect Polish air space, most recently as part of the NATO mission Enhanced Air Policing North (eAPN) in Malbork.

A German air force Eurofighter Typhoon taking off in December 2025 from the Polish military airbase in Malbork Image: Adam Warøawa/PAP/dpa/picture alliance

Questions of military cooperation were also prioritized in the closing statement that followed German-Polish intergovernmental consultations on December 1, 2025. The process culminated in the signing of the German-Polish defense agreement on June 17, 2026.

On August 15 this year, three German planes, two Eurofighters and an A400M transport aircraft, participated in the celebration of Polish Armed Forces Day. The head of the German air force, Holger Neumann, was one of the guests of honor. Some American GIs marched in the military parade ― but no German soldiers.

Kaczynski: No German soldiers in Poland

However, not all the political forces in Poland are happy about this new Polish-German brotherhood-in-arms. Memories of the trauma of World War II are still very much alive in Polish society and are regularly instrumentalized by the right-wing conservative Law and Justice Party (PiS) to stir up anti-German feeling.

Back in 2014, PiS leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski said he didn't want any German soldiers in Poland.

"It will be at least seven generations before that is acceptable," he said.

The line of anti-tank obstacles forming part of the East Shield near Budry in Poland Image: Jacek Lepiarz/DW

In the fall of 2022, when the German government offered to relocate two German Patriot batteries to Poland after an incident involving a Ukrainian rocket gone astray, the PiS government blocked the move.

"Germany's previous behavior gives us no reason to believe that it will decide to fire on the Russian rockets," Kaczynski declared.

Just last March, Poland's president Karol Nawrocki, who is backed by the PiS, vetoed legislation that would have allowed Poland to access almost 44 billion euros (55 billion dollars) in EU defense loans because German armaments companies could also have benefited.

Poland sees the US as the most important guarantor of its security, and is trying to establish a special relationship with Washington. Around 10,000 US soldiers are currently stationed in various places around the country. Warsaw is keen to establish a permanent military base on its territory: Until now, a significant number of the US soldiers are in Poland on rotation.

This article has been translated from German.

World.title: France issues warning over thousands of substandard condoms
World.content:
French anti-fraud and health agencies have issued a recall order for roughly 260,000 condoms. They advised users to consider sexually transmitted infection and pregnancy tests amid risks of bursting or perforations.

France's anti-fraud and health agencies issued a joint statement on Friday saying they were recalling more than a quarter of a million condoms that could be defective.

It said that the majority were sold online via major marketplaces by Asian vendors.

What did the government agencies say about the potentially substandard condoms?

Of the roughly 260,000 contraceptives being recalled, authorities said around 1,000 boxes, or 40,000 individual condoms, had already been sold.

"Laboratory analyses identified two non-compliant products, characterized by a risk of bursting and, in one case, the presence of perforations," authorities said.

The anti-fraud agency, the DGCCRF, and the DGS health agency said in a joint statement that the condoms lacked the required CE marking that designates a product conforms with the standards of the European Economic Area trading zone.

Even novelty and seasonal condoms should carry the CE marking Image: Michael Bihlmayer/CHROMORANGE/picture alliance

"The identified condoms lack a CE marking, third-party conformity assessment, and — in most cases — packaging in French," the government agencies said. "Consequently, they are deemed non-compliant and potentially pose serious risks to user health and safety (such as sexually transmitted infections and unintended pregnancies)."

The statement advised people who had used the condoms to get screened for sexually transmitted infections and to take a pregnancy test if they had any reason to be suspicious such as a missed or late period.

The government said the online vendors had agreed to remove the affected listings and to send in the recalled products.

The statement listed two brands of condoms made by a Japanese company, Okamoto Industries, and the brands MyLubie and Friday Bae by Passage du Desir.

France offers people aged up to 25 free condoms via pharmacies without a prescription in a bid to prevent STIs and unwanted pregnancies.

Young people in France are mostly eligible for free condoms from pharmacies without a prescription under a policy initiated during Emmanuel Macron's presidency Image: Aurore Marechal/ABACA/picture alliance

World.title: El Gobierno prepara un plan económico para revitalizar Ceuta tras la crisis migratoria
World.content:
Cuerpo viajará a reunirse con distintos sectores para ver sus necesidades. El Consejo de Ministros aprobará este martes 25 millones para atender a los menores, pero habrá goteo de más dinero en las próximas citas

El Gobierno parece ser muy consciente de que la crisis de Ceuta le ha abierto un agujero de credibilidad importante. Todos los esfuerzos del Ejecutivo durante este verano, que en un principio se pusieron sobre los durísimos incendios de julio, se han concentrado en intentar dar una solución a una crisis humanitaria que está lejos de ser resuelta, con miles de inmigrantes aún por las calles de la ciudad autónoma, y tratar de volver a la normalidad.

Desde el presidente a media docena de ministros han viajado allí intentando buscar soluciones, de momento con resultados que discute sobre todo el gobierno de la ciudad, en manos del PP, que insiste en que hay que expulsar a todos los que entraron el 30 y 31 de julio, algo muy difícil de ejecutar con la legislación vigente con los adultos e imposible en el caso de los menores, al menos a corto plazo.

Pero además de atender la emergencia, el Ejecutivo trabaja ya en el medio plazo y La Moncloa le ha pedido a todos los ministerios con competencias más directas sobre la crisis que le envíen ideas y peticiones para un gran plan de recuperación de Ceuta en los próximos meses, sobre el que se está trabajando sobre todo en La Moncloa y en Economía.

Un barrendero y clientes en terrazas, el jueves en Ceuta. Joaquin Sanchez

La ciudad, que tiene un atractivo turístico importante y recibe miles de visitantes todos los años, también los que van en viaje camino a Marruecos, ha quedado marcada por unas imágenes de 80.000 inmigrantes entrando a nado que han viajado por muchos países ―Donald Trump y Elon Musk tardaron muy poco en comentarlas para burlarse de las políticas proinmigración de España―.

Para tratar de darle la vuelta a esta situación y a esa imagen, que tiene la economía de la ciudad muy tocada en las últimas semanas, especialmente el comercio y el turismo, el Gobierno prepara ya un plan de reactivación con una cantidad aún no cerrada, pero que para una ciudad de algo más de 80.000 habitantes será importante, según distintas fuentes del Ejecutivo.

Algunas cuantificaciones iniciales con las que trabaja el Ejecutivo hablan de al menos 15 millones de euros para reactivar el comercio, con rebajas de impuestos y reducciones de cotizaciones a la seguridad social y medidas similares, además de ayudas directas para compensar el lucro cesante durante todo este periodo de crisis en la ciudad, en la que los vecinos prácticamente se han quedado en sus casas y no ha habido apenas visitantes, con lo que el comercio se ha desplomado. Habrá también un plan de turismo y se está trabajando con más ayudas para un proyecto ya en marcha que utiliza agua desalada en Ceuta.

El vicepresidente primero, Carlos Cuerpo, tiene previsto desplazarse a la ciudad la próxima semana, aunque aún no están cerrados los detalles, para hablar con los representantes de los afectados y detallar más concretamente sus necesidades para terminar de perfilar ese plan.

El grueso del dinero no irá pues presumiblemente en este primer Consejo de Ministros tras el parón veraniego, el 25 de agosto, sino en forma de goteo y con distintos decretos a lo largo de las próximas semanas, como sucedió con otras crisis como la dana en Valencia, pero esta primera cita del martes sí estará totalmente dominada por la crisis de Ceuta.

La portavoz y ministra de Inclusión, que incluye la competencia de Migraciones, Elma Saiz, ha estado casi toda la semana en Ceuta y podrá dar cuenta de la situación y de las gestiones que se están haciendo al Consejo de Ministros y a los ciudadanos en la rueda de prensa posterior, que estará con toda probabilidad centrada en Ceuta, un asunto que la oposición ha visto como una gran oportunidad de desgastar al Gobierno.

La ministra de Juventud e Infancia, Sira Rego, llevará a la reunión la aprobación de un fondo de 25 millones de euros para los menores de Ceuta, con el que podrá financiar el traslado de 500 niñas a la Península que rechaza de momento el PP, pero que el Ejecutivo confía en que el Gobierno de la ciudad acepte porque ahora mismo no es viable devolver a los menores a Marruecos ―la ley del menor y la de extranjería exigen garantías muy claras y estudios individualizados de los casos que tardan meses, y el Tribunal Supremo sentenció que no se pueden devolver sin más aunque Marruecos esté de acuerdo y la Audiencia Provincial de Cádiz inhabilitó a la exdelegada del Gobierno y la exvicepresidenta de Ceuta por hacerlo―. El Gobierno ya activó seis millones de euros para hacer frente a la emergencia humanitaria, pero habrá más fondos para atender a los inmigrantes.

Vista de una céntrica calle de Ceuta, el jueves. Joaquin Sanchez

También hay un plan en marcha para reforzar el sistema judicial en Ceuta, presionado estos días por el proceso de expulsiones y peticiones de asilo de miles de personas. El Ministerio de Justicia ya explicó que ha aumentado hasta un 271% la capacidad operativa del Instituto de Medicina Legal y Ciencias Forenses; hay dos plazas de refuerzo para el tribunal de instancia, y se gestionarán más con el CGPJ, otra de médico forense, tres refuerzos en la fiscalía y cinco letrados nuevos para el turno de oficio, además de tres fiscales sustitutos que ya están autorizados. También se están preparando refuerzos importantes en sanidad, aunque la ministra Mónica García ha insistido en que los ceutíes no están viviendo una crisis sanitaria, porque aún hay plazas en el hospital, pero sí hay que atender una emergencia en la que el hacinamiento de los inmigrantes está derivando en la extensión de enfermedades como la sarna.

Otra de las cuestiones que están encima de la mesa para mejorar la situación en Ceuta y sobre todo la seguridad de la frontera es la de construir una protección más estable que la actual en el agua. Es un proyecto del que se ha hablado muchas veces, pero nunca se ha realizado. Ahora, después del último salto masivo, en el que murieron más de 100 inmigrantes, se ha instalado una barrera flotante, pero es una solución temporal que no sirve cuando lleguen los temporales del otoño y el invierno. Por eso está prevista una obra de ingeniería más estable para continuar la protección fronteriza en el agua. Todo esto también supondrá un desembolso importante.

La intención política también es que las dotaciones extra de policías y guardias civiles que hay en Ceuta desde que estalló la crisis —330 policías y 240 guardias civiles nuevos, que en total, con los que ya había, suman 1.659 miembros de los cuerpos y fuerzas de seguridad del Estado desplegados allí— se instalen en la ciudad de forma permanente para reforzar la dotación.

El Ejecutivo admite que la situación es muy complicada, sobre todo hasta que todas las personas que están por las calles estén controladas en los centros de estancia temporal que se están habilitando, pero distintas fuentes insisten en que no hay una situación de descontrol de seguridad como plantean los sindicatos policiales y que sí hay aumento de delitos pero, teniendo en cuenta que Ceuta es una ciudad habitualmente muy segura, la situación no está fuera de control.

Problema mayúsculo

En cualquier caso, el Ejecutivo parece tener muy claro que la crisis de Ceuta es un problema mayúsculo, tal vez el principal que tiene ahora Pedro Sánchez encima de la mesa, y distintos miembros del Gobierno consultados señalan que se está poniendo ahí todo el foco con dinero y medios materiales y humanos para resolver cuanto antes la situación. También se trabaja en Exteriores para garantizar con Marruecos que algo así no vuelva a suceder.

Fuentes del Gobierno reivindican la actitud de Marruecos el pasado 15 de agosto, cuando desbarató un segundo intento de salto masivo organizado en las redes sociales, y confían en que esta crisis sirva como aprendizaje para evitar un nuevo salto. Cuando se les pregunta si en 2021, cuando saltaron más de 10.000 personas, no se había pensado ya que esto no volvería a pasar, señalan que en aquella crisis Marruecos sí dejó claro que se trataba de una represalia por la acogida al líder saharaui Brahim Gali en un hospital español, pero esta vez Rabat insiste en que ellos no están detrás de esta operación y no tienen ningún conflicto con el Gobierno español que reprochar, ni siquiera el viaje de Sánchez a Argelia, que estaba hablado con el país vecino.

El Gobierno trabaja así en tres ejes a la vez: gestiones diplomáticas y de refuerzo de seguridad para que no vuelva a suceder un salto masivo, gestión de la crisis humanitaria con una solución para adultos y menores mientras se tramitan devoluciones y expulsiones, y plan de recuperación económica de Ceuta. Todos ellos requieren tiempo, pero la presión es enorme por parte de los ciudadanos, especialmente los ceutíes, de la oposición, de la justicia, de la policía e incluso de los socios europeos, muy pendientes de la solución de esta crisis en la frontera más caliente de la UE.

World.title: Correr, nadar o pedalear, ¿suponen el mismo esfuerzo y logran los mismos efectos?
World.content:
En estas fechas de verano es común iniciar el proceso de ponerse en forma, ya sea con un familiar o con un grupo de amigos. Es habitual renovar la ropa deportiva y activarse, ya sea con la bicicleta, en la montaña o para desplazarse al trabajo; en la piscina, porque en el agua no duelen las articulaciones; o salir a correr, por la sensación de libertad. La realidad es que las tres actividades permiten moverse y ejercitarse, aunque el cuerpo no tiene la misma respuesta ante cada una de ellas. En un primer momento nos puede parecer un esfuerzo aeróbico equivalente, pero la realidad es que correr, nadar y pedalear son buenos para la salud, pero tienen efectos diferentes a nivel cardiovascular, óseo y muscular, así como en la propia adherencia al ejercicio físico.

Las tres actividades imponen una demanda aeróbica y mejoran claramente la condición física cuando se practican con regularidad. Pero no hay una mejor que otra desde el punto de vista de la salud. Son opciones válidas para movernos. En un estudio realizado en el Reino Unido con una muestra de 80.000 adultos, se pudo observar que tanto la práctica del ciclismo como la natación se asociaban a una menor tasa de mortalidad por diferentes causas, y en el caso de la natación también con una menor mortalidad cardiovascular. Un resultado interesante fue que la carrera no mostraba una asociación estadísticamente significativa, reflejando que los efectos son diferentes en función de la persona, la frecuencia, la intensidad y el tiempo que se lleva practicando.

La imagen de personas corriendo en diferentes superficies como arena, césped, asfalto o las aceras refleja una diferencia con nadar y pedalear, que es el impacto. Al correr estamos apoyando nuestro peso corporal de manera repetida contra el suelo, donde la carga mecánica generada ayuda a estimular huesos, músculos y tendones, pero a su vez puede generar demasiada carga en articulaciones, especialmente si la técnica de carrera no es la adecuada, no se realiza progresivamente o siempre sobre superficies muy duras o inestables en los apoyos. Es fundamental para mantener los huesos saludables y fuertes el estímulo mecánico, por ello, en este sentido, la carrera es más beneficiosa que nadar o pedalear, donde el cuerpo no soporta todo nuestro peso.

La natación estaría en el extremo opuesto, donde la flotabilidad en el agua reduce la carga sobre las articulaciones, con un menor impacto y estrés mecánico. Esta actividad supone un gran recurso para ejercitarse para personas mayores, embarazadas, personas con obesidad, artritis o molestias musculoesqueléticas. No debemos olvidar que en el agua, la resistencia se ejerce en todas las direcciones con un esfuerzo muscular continuo en cada brazada y patada. Sin embargo, esta ausencia de impacto hace que la natación no sea el mejor ejercicio para el aumento de la densidad mineral ósea. La evidencia científica indica que el medio acuático ofrece ventajas únicas desde el punto de vista cardiovascular y funcional, aunque no sustituye los beneficios osteogénicos de las actividades con carga.

Por otro lado, los estudios sobre los beneficios de pedalear refieren mejoras consistentes en la capacidad cardiorrespiratoria y una reducción del riesgo cardiovascular al usarse de manera habitual. Pedalear se encuentra en el punto medio entre las tres actividades, ya que requiere una gran participación del sistema cardiovascular, pero no implica demasiado impacto articular. Esta suele ser la razón por la que mucha gente prefiere pedalear a correr, sobre todo si tiene sobrepeso, dolor en la rodilla o quiere ir aumentando progresivamente los minutos de práctica. Además, pedalear es un recurso diario que permite ir a trabajar, a la universidad o a comprar, tal y como es común en los Países Bajos.

Sin embargo, pedalear no es la única solución, en quienes se ejercitan con volúmenes elevados (o profesionalmente), los estudios científicos se asocian a una menor densidad mineral ósea, debido a ese menor impacto. Este aspecto indica que no hay una única actividad que pueda cubrir todas las necesidades que requiere el organismo. Por ello, siempre que se ejercite muchas horas en la bicicleta o nadando, se podría beneficiar de un complemento con ejercicios de fuerza, mientras que un corredor necesitaría como complemento el trabajo de fuerza y movilidad como medio de prevención de lesiones.

Nadar añade otro aspecto, ya que modifica la respuesta fisiológica al estar el cuerpo en horizontal, facilitando el retorno venoso, aumentando el volumen sanguíneo y reduciendo la frecuencia cardíaca para un esfuerzo percibido similar. Además, el agua ofrece resistencia que incrementa el gasto energético al nadar más rápido. Este hecho puede hacer que dos personas naden la misma distancia, pero experimenten esfuerzos muy diferentes según la técnica que tengan al nadar; un experto puede nadar con mayor facilidad y un principiante puede agotarse en poco tiempo.

En este punto, el lector puede preguntarse: ¿cuál de las tres sería mejor? Siendo honestos, depende. El objetivo de las tres busca la mejora cardiovascular, pero si hay dolor articular o sobrepeso, nadar o pedalear son más agradables para la persona; si hay preocupación por la salud ósea, no se debe nadar o pedalear de manera exclusiva; si se quiere una actividad sencilla y económica, correr será la más adecuada.

El debate no debe estar en qué actividad es mejor o superior; lo ideal sería elegir aquella o aquellas que permitan ejercitarse y mantenerlo a lo largo de los años. Son tres formas distintas de moverse, tres respuestas fisiológicas diferentes y un mismo objetivo: seguir en movimiento. La mejor elección no será la misma para todos, pero casi siempre será aquella que se pueda seguir practicando dentro de 10 o 20 años. Recordemos que el movimiento es vida.

World.title: Italia quiere poner orden en el caos de sus 12.000 playas privadas: más transparencia y nuevas tasas
World.content:
Entre el 33% y el 42% de los arenales del país son de pago. El Gobierno de Meloni, presionado por Bruselas, abrirá a concurso su gestión

Italia presume de sus 8.000 kilómetros de costa, pero disfrutar de ellos no siempre es gratis. Mientras que en otras partes ir a la playa significa buscar un hueco en la arena, en Italia la experiencia suele ser muy distinta. Encontrar un espacio donde plantar la sombrilla sin pagar puede convertirse en toda una aventura. En amplios tramos del litoral, el acceso al mar está gestionado por empresas privadas, mediante concesiones públicas, que han transformado las playas en un negocio multimillonario. El resultado es una de las estampas más características del verano italiano: bosques interminables de sombrillas perfectamente alineadas, acompañadas de sus respectivas tumbonas, esperando a ser alquiladas por precios que pueden superar los 35 euros al día.

Este modelo, muy arraigado en el país y marcado por una gestión plagada de irregularidades, afronta una reforma que lleva años aplazándose a pesar de la presión de Bruselas para poner orden. Las playas gestionadas por concesionarios privados no han dejado de ganar terreno. Según la asociación ecologista italiana Legambiente, ocupan ya más del 42% de los arenales del país. El Ministerio de Infraestructuras rebaja esa cifra al 33%, una diferencia que se explica por el criterio utilizado para el cálculo: el Gobierno utiliza para sus cuentas toda la línea costera italiana y no únicamente las zonas aptas para el baño.

Desde hace décadas, las empresas, casi siempre familiares —las concesiones suelen heredarse—, pagan cánones relativamente bajos al Estado por explotar espacios públicos, mientras los precios para los usuarios han aumentado de forma exponencial. Las concesionarias gestionan los servicios como los baños, las duchas, los vestuarios, los aparcamientos, además del alquiler de sombrillas y tumbonas. También controlan los chiringuitos y cafeterías y se encargan de las labores de salvamento. Mientras que las zonas públicas suelen estar descuidadas, a menudo sucias, y desprovistas de servicios públicos.

Se trata de un asunto sensible que divide a la opinión pública italiana. Para unos, las playas de pago garantizan orden, limpieza y comodidad; para otros, representan la privatización de un bien público que debería ser accesible para todos. La principal crítica al sistema es la enorme diferencia entre lo que pagan las concesionarias por explotar las playas y los beneficios que obtienen. El Estado recauda entre 80 y 100 millones de euros al año por las concesiones, mientras que el sector, marcado por la opacidad, mueve más de 2.000 millones de euros anuales, según distintas estimaciones. El propio Tribunal de Cuentas italiano ha advertido de que los cánones abonados por los empresarios no suelen ser proporcionales a los ingresos que obtienen.

Uno de los aspectos más controvertidos del modelo italiano es que las concesiones se han renovado durante años casi por inercia. Sin concursos abiertos ni una competencia efectiva y sin controles ni transparencia, los mismos operadores han conservado la explotación de amplios tramos del litoral público durante generaciones, consolidando un sistema difícil de encontrar en otros países europeos.

Un paso adelante

Bruselas lleva años reclamando cambios. La Comisión considera que Italia incumple la directiva Bolkestein de 2009, que obliga a garantizar la libre competencia en la adjudicación de este tipo de concesiones, y ha presionado repetidamente a Roma. Tras décadas de aplazamientos y enfrentamientos, el Gobierno de Giorgia Meloni ha abordado la cuestión. La reforma aprobada prevé que para el 30 de septiembre de 2027 salgan a concurso público todas las playas de pago, unas 12.000 repartidas por todo el país. Además, las concesiones tendrán una duración limitada, de entre cinco y 20 años, y habrá compensaciones económicas para los actuales titulares por las inversiones y obras que hayan realizado.

La perspectiva de abrir el mercado ha despertado, sin embargo, inquietud entre muchos empresarios del sector, que temen que los concursos favorezcan la entrada de grandes grupos turísticos o fondos de inversión capaces de desplazar a los negocios familiares que tradicionalmente han dominado las costas italianas.

World.title: Adiós lavanda, hola girasoles: un viaje por Burgos cuando en agosto cambia de color
World.content:
Cuando los tonos morados desaparecen de los campos, el amarillo toma el relevo en la comarca de La Bureba o la Ribera del Duero, con Briviesca, Poza de la Sal y Caleruega como paradas principales para descubrir el patrimonio burgalés

En agosto, Burgos cambia el perfume por la luz. Al recorrer los campos de la provincia por carreteras secundarias y caminos, el viajero aprecia una muda de color: la lavanda que en julio pinta hectáreas de morado deja paso a los girasoles, que colorean de amarillo vastas extensiones de La Bureba y algunos paisajes de la Ribera del Duero.

Quien quiera rodearse de miles de girasoles —esas flores que Van Gogh volvió universales— debe acudir durante esta época del año a La Bureba. Allí los girasoles aparecen a los lados de las carreteras, y se convierten en uno de los grandes protagonistas del paisaje durante unas semanas. Caminar junto a los campos en su momento más vigoroso puede justificar por sí solo la visita a esta comarca y sus pueblos.

Más información Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj

El mejor punto de partida para entender el paisaje estival de esta comarca burgalesa, que, además, fue de las primeras en adquirir personalidad dentro del condado castellano, es la localidad de Briviesca. En esta época del año los girasoles se muestran en su máximo esplendor y embellecen aún más al pueblo. Briviesca invita a detenerse y mirar los campos más allá de su condición de cultivo. La iniciativa Girasoles con Arte, puesta en marcha en 2024, combina el patrimonio urbano de Briviesca y el paisaje agrícola mediante dos trazados sencillos: uno de 1,63 kilómetros y otro de 2,67 kilómetros.

La plaza Mayor de Briviesca, en la provincia de Burgos. Teo Moreno Moreno (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Quienes deseen conocer más a fondo el ambiente local en torno a los girasoles pueden combinar paseos junto a ese paisaje efímero con una visita más detenida por el pueblo. La propuesta puede realizarse en medio día, y se puede iniciar con una etapa más urbana. Esta se desarrolla a lo largo de distintos puntos de interés de la localidad conocida como La Bien Trazada, por su plano ortogonal con forma de tablero de ajedrez. Comienza en la plaza Mayor, el punto desde el que la localidad muestra su trazado rectilíneo. En el centro se levanta un templete musical de estilo modernista construido en 1909. La siguiente parada está a escasos metros, en la excolegiata de Santa María la Mayor, iniciada en el siglo XIV y reformada en el siglo XVIII. La ruta continúa hacia el monasterio de Santa Clara, cuyo interior alberga un retablo de más de 20 metros de altura, tallado en madera de nogal y singular por carecer de policromía. La ausencia de color permite apreciar la minuciosidad de la talla, que bajo una capa de policromía podría haberse relegado a un segundo plano. Esa falta de acabado, atribuida a problemas económicos, terminó por convertirse en una de sus particularidades más reconocibles.

Retablo mayor en la nave central de la Iglesia de Santa Clara. Miguel Sotomayor (GETTY IMAGES)

Pero el encanto del girasol en La Bureba no se queda solo en Briviesca. El viaje continúa hacia Poza de la Sal, un recorrido que lleva al viajero a través de extensas hectáreas doradas cercanas a los pueblos de Quintanabureba y Llano de Bureba. En Poza de la Sal, el amarillo del verano encuentra un contrapunto mineral e histórico: una villa encaramada al borde de la llanura, con el castillo de los Rojas en lo alto y las antiguas salinas hundidas en el diapiro que dio nombre al pueblo. Conocida también como el Balcón de la Bureba, permite una vista amplia sobre la llanura de la comarca antes de volver a la carretera.

Un campo de girasoles cerca de Poza de la Sal. Architect´s Eye / Alamy / Cordon PRess

Al sur de la provincia, el amarillo cambia de compañía. Mientras que en La Bureba crece junto a cereales y llanuras, en la Ribera florece entre viñas y el recuerdo reciente de la lavanda. Después de la siega, la lavanda permanece en aceites esenciales, aguas florales, jabones, perfumes y otros productos elaborados en la zona. Así, Caleruega y Cilleruelo de Arriba han empezado a construir en el sur burgalés una pequeña cultura alrededor de esta planta.

Una calle en la localidad burgalesa de Poza de la Sal. Jose Luis Alvarez Esteban (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien se acerque a Caleruega para seguir el rastro dorado en los terrenos que circundan al pueblo entrará también en un lugar que no se entiende sin su más ilustre personaje: Santo Domingo de Guzmán, patrón provincial. Al llegar al casco urbano, el Torreón de los Guzmanes se yergue con 17 metros de altura desde época medieval sobre el resto de la arquitectura local. Le acompaña el Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, fundado en 1266 por mandato del rey Alfonso X el Sabio, que en su interior alberga un claustro gótico y el Pocito de Santo Domingo, donde la tradición sitúa el nacimiento del santo y al que se atribuyen propiedades milagrosas. En lo alto del casco urbano, la iglesia de San Sebastián, de piedra románica, vigila la plaza mayor del pueblo desde el siglo XII. De esta parroquia procede la pila donde fue bautizado Santo Domingo, trasladada fuera de Caleruega y utilizada en bautizos de miembros de la Casa Real española desde 1605.

El claustro del Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, en la localidad de Caleruega. Blanca Saenz de Castillo (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien quiera detenerse más tiempo en la zona encontrará, además de los campos de girasoles que acompañan algunas carreteras de acceso, otros puntos de interés. El Sendero de las Loberas, de 10,2 kilómetros, permite acercarse a esas construcciones circulares de piedra que servían para resguardar el ganado de los lobos. En el entorno de Caleruega también aparecen otros vestigios, como los yacimientos arqueológicos de San Mamés y La Pudia o la Bodega de Alfonso VIII, vinculada al despoblado de San Martín de Bañuelos.

La ruta en busca de más hectáreas doradas por el sur de Burgos puede prolongarse por la Ribera hacia el pueblo vecino de Baños de Valdearados. Allí, la Villa Romana de Santa Cruz recuerda la huella de Roma en el territorio, mientras que a finales de agosto la fiesta en honor a Baco, dios romano del vino, llena el pueblo de togas, desfiles, mercado y vino de la Ribera (este año se celebra el 22 y 23 de agosto).

Celebración de la Fiesta a Baco, en Baños de Valdearados. Carlos Mora (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Otra parada cercana es Villanueva de Gumiel, que permite prolongar esa continuación amarilla del verano por los campos de la Ribera. En sus calles se aprecian las fachadas de las casas antiguas, con una arquitectura caracterizada por plantas bajas de mampostería de piedra y plantas altas de entramado de madera y adobe. La iglesia de San Mamés, del siglo XVII, se diferencia de otras formas tradicionales al estructurarse en dos naves simétricas con ocho arcos cruzados y un valioso retablo del siglo XVI.

Recorrer con calma estos pueblos burgaleses permite disfrutar de un manto dorado que parece no agotarse desde la carretera. En estas tierras, la floración suele regalar sus mejores imágenes entre finales de julio y agosto. Y a quienes busquen mejores fotos suele convenirles acercarse al amanecer, momento en el que los rayos de sol iluminan de frente las cabezas maduras que miran hacia el este.

Como en toda floración agrícola, el estado de cada parcela cambia según la siembra, el calor y el momento de cosecha, por lo que conviene consultar con las oficinas de turismo antes de emprender la ruta. Y, sobre todo, conviene recordar algo crucial: estos campos no existen para la foto, son cultivos en activo. Hay que respetar todas las flores para que el siguiente visitante pueda admirar los campos de esta Castilla con la misma belleza.

World.title: Dutch privacy watchdog fines Uber €825m over drivers’ rights
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Dutch data protection authority AP has fined Uber €825 million for deactivating drivers’ accounts through automated systems without properly informing them, in what is the second-largest penalty ever issued under European privacy law.

The watchdog leads on privacy oversight of Uber across the EU because the company’s European head office is in Amsterdam.

Under the EU’s data protection rules, companies are not allowed to let an algorithm alone take decisions that significantly affect someone’s life. A human must be involved, and the person affected must be able to object.

The case relates to events between 2020 and 2022 and began with complaints from drivers in France, who had been suspended on suspicion of fraud, such as taking unnecessary detours to increase their fares.

Uber to appeal

Uber said it would challenge the fine. “We strongly disagree with this decision and disproportionate fine,” a spokesperson told Reuters, adding that the company took drivers’ rights seriously.

The firm said its current policies included human review and allowed drivers to contest suspensions, and that it no longer deactivated accounts permanently through automated systems alone.

The penalty easily exceeds the AP’s previous record, a €290 million fine imposed on Uber last year for transferring drivers’ data to the United States.

That case, which Uber is also appealing, grew out of the same complaints by French drivers. The regulator had already fined the company €10 million in early 2024 over drivers’ privacy rights and €600,000 in 2018.

The only larger fine under the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is the €1.2 billion penalty handed to Meta by Ireland’s regulator in 2023, for transferring European Facebook users’ data to the United States, a case that Meta is appealing.

World.title: Wall Street Journal tips Groningen novelist for Nobel prize
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Wall Street Journal has named the Groningen-based novelist Anjet Daanje a serious contender for the Nobel prize in literature, in a review of her novel Het lied van ooievaar en dromedaris (The Song of Stork and Dromedary), first published in 2022 and recently translated to English.

The paper’s critic Sam Sacks said Daanje is “one of the continent’s leading writers.”

Sacks noted that the prize has never gone to a writer from the Netherlands, which he put down to bad luck rather than any lack of quality. He named the late Harry Mulisch as another Dutch author who deserved it.

The last Dutch author nominated was Simon Vestdijk, who received multiple nominations in the 1950s and 60s. The Nobel archive is sealed for 50 years, so any more recent candidates remain secret.

Inspired by the Brontës

Daanje, who was born in Drenthe, achieved a breakthrough with her novel Deherdenking soldaat (The Remembered Soldier) in 2019.

Het lied van ooievaar en dromedaris won both the Libris literature prize and the Boekenbon prize – the first book to take the Netherlands’ two main literary awards. Daanje went on to receive the Constantijn Huygens prize for her body of work.

The English edition runs to more than 700 pages. Loosely based on the Brontë sisters, it circles an Emily Brontë-like writer through interlinked stories spanning almost three centuries.

The 2026 Nobel prize in literature will be announced in Stockholm on October 8.

World.title: Cabinet still aims for majority budget support, Heinen says
World.content:
The Dutch cabinet still believes it can win support from across the political spectrum for its annual budget, finance minister Eelco Heinen has said, a week before the plans are due to be sent off for review.

“I’m confident that will work out,” Heinen told reporters ahead of Friday’s cabinet meeting. “We’re now really in the final phase.” He said he believed the opposition parties whose votes are needed are moving closer together and “don’t differ that much from each other.”

Heinen, who stayed away from the opening days of talks with opposition leaders this week, is now holding his own discussions with the parties. The cabinet wants a deal in place by next Friday, August 28, when it plans to send the budget to the Council of State.

Left or right

The minority coalition of D66, VVD and CDA is 10 seats short of a majority in the lower house and holds less than a third of the seats in the senate, leaving it reliant on opposition votes.

Support from opposition party PRO, which has 20 seats, would give it a comfortable majority, while a deal with the far-right JA21, which has nine seats, would leave it one short and dependent on a third party.

PRO, JA21 and the orthodox Protestant SGP have all said the cabinet will eventually have to choose between a majority on the left or on the right. But Heinen has resisted that, backing a call this week by Christian-social ChristenUnie leader Mirjam Bikker for the parties to drop the left-right divide and judge the plans on their merits.

Welfare cuts

Talks with PRO, the most straightforward route to a majority, remain difficult. After a meeting on Thursday, the party’s finance spokesperson Luc Stultiens said he had seen little movement “and that will be needed if you want our support.”

PRO wants the cabinet to scrap €6.5 billion in planned cuts to social security and raise the money through higher taxes on wealth and corporations instead. Its position is backed by the unions, which have called a national public transport strike on September 9 in protest at the reforms.

JA21 and the SGP, which are working together, met ministers again on Friday morning, with the ChristenUnie due later in the day. The budget is set to be presented on Prinsjesdag, September 15.

World.title: Government condemns Israeli West Bank settlement plan
World.content:
The Netherlands has joined six other governments in condemning Israel’s decision to open bidding on a major settlement project in the occupied West Bank, and called on the Netanyahu regime to withdraw the plans immediately.

Prime minister Rob Jetten and the leaders of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Norway called the project “unacceptable” in a joint statement, and said they have “grave concerns” over the potential impact it could have on achieving peace in the region, particularly amid “unprecedented levels of violence by settlers against civilians.”

Israel’s construction and housing ministry opened bidding on Tuesday for 1,234 homes, part of a wider plan for 3,401 settler homes in E1, an area east of Jerusalem. Contractors have until October 19 to bid, a week before Israeli elections.

Critics say the project would split the West Bank in two and cut East Jerusalem off from it, making a contiguous Palestinian state impossible.

The condemnation comes as the Netherlands prepares to enforce its own ban on settlement goods, which takes effect on September 22. The three-year measure bars the import, sale and trade of goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories.

The Netherlands is also the main EU entry point for produce grown in Israeli settlements, according to research published in June, handling around a third of such shipments reaching the bloc.

Settlements in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law. The E1 plan, approved last year, faces a legal challenge in Israel, where a court has asked the state to respond to the petitions by September 1.

World.title: Police shooting in Sittard wounds Nijmegen man
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Police in Sittard in Limburg shot a man outside the city’s police station on Stationsplein overnight Friday due to what they called a “suspicious situation”.

The suspect, a 34-year-old man from Nijmegen, was injured in the leg and received first aid on the scene. He was then arrested and transferred to hospital.

Police shootings are rare in the Netherlands. Last year, officers shot at people 15 times.

Still, the national police are investigating the incident, as all cases involving an officer shooting that results in injury or death must be looked into.

Police are also looking into the cause and background of the incident.

World.title: New medicine gives hope to Dutch narcolepsy sufferers
World.content:
Some 8,000 Dutch people suffer from narcolepsy, a sleep disorder that leaves sufferers spontaneously falling asleep during the day.

Now, for the first time, a new drug approved earlier this month in the US is being touted as the first to target the disease’s roots rather than its symptoms.

“I have been trying to give people a reasonable life for 40 years,” Gert Jan Lammers, special professor of sleep disorders at Leiden University Medical Centre, told broadcaster NOS. “With this medicine, we finally saw real improvement.”

Several of his patients participated in the drug’s research trials, and he says the results are positive. “People feel normal again. I’ve been working on this for 40 years now and I haven’t seen this before. It doesn’t work perfectly for everyone, and it doesn’t work all day, but it’s fundamentally different from what we’ve been able to do so far.”

The drug, Orzeyful (oveporexton) still has to be approved by the European Medicines Agency before being prescribed in the Netherlands, which will likely not happen until at least the end of next year.

But for those who have taken it, including Dutch trial participants who can continue using it before its approval here, it’s been a life-changer.

“It’s like you’re finally getting a good pair of glasses,” says Leontien Sickenga, who has taken the drug for one and one-half years. “With other medication I saw the world a bit better, but with this medication the world is clear. When I’m awake, I’m really there.”

In addition to falling asleep in the day, Sickenga also suffered from muscle relaxation and sleep paralysis, common in narcolepsy patients. “It’s very drastic,” she said.

How it works

According to the US Food and Drug Administration, narcolepsy “is caused by the loss of brain cells that produce orexin, a chemical messenger that regulates wakefulness, sleep, and muscle tone.”

Without orexin, the brain has trouble controlling the boundaries between sleep and waking, resulting in narcolepsy’s debilitating symptoms. But the new drug, rather than trying to relieve those symptoms, “directly activates the same brain receptor that the body’s own orexin would normally stimulate, restoring the missing signal.”

Professor of sleep diagnostics Sebastiaan Overeem, who was not involved in the drug’s research, is positive. “This is fundamentally new and very promising,” he says. “Of course, there are no miracle cures, and we still have to see how this drug works in the long run. But in the field, everyone is impressed.”

Side effects of the drug include urinating more, and it’s not yet known how effective it will be in the long-term.

“I don’t want to be too positive, because some things we can’t know yet” says Lammers. “But so far, all the signals are on green.”

World.title: Frisian asylum center to remain open, frustrating locals
World.content:
The ministry of justice and security informed the municipality of De Fryske Marren earlier this week that the asylum seekers’ centre in Balk, which was due to permanently shut its doors on October 1 2026, will remain open for another three years, upsetting local officials.

“For the municipal executive, the following applies: a deal is a deal,” says the municipality’s website. “The fact that the agreements cannot be fulfilled now causes disappointment and frustration.”

And, reports Omrop Fryslân, will lead to legal action.

The asylum centre opened in 2016 for what was supposed to be five years. That period was extended several times, most recently in 2024, when a deal was also made to reduce the number of refugees living in the centre from 500 to 225.

While the number of asylum seekers has been reduced, refugee settlement agency COA said the lack of alternative shelters means it can’t meet the October closure deadline.

Closure not an option

“We have been looking for other solutions for as long as possible”, said COA’s Joeri Kapteijns. “However, we have the legal and social responsibility to welcome and guide people safely and with dignity. As a result, closure without an alternative is not an option.”

Closing the Balk shelter, said COA, would “mean that 300 people, families and children, will be on the streets.”

The municipality says it doesn’t want to see people on the streets, but it’s unacceptable that the deal has been broken.

“Although De Fryske Marren wants to prevent residents from being left without suitable shelter from a human point of view, it does not accept this situation,” said the municipality. “The responsibility for the residents and replacement shelter lies primarily with COA.”

But COA says the nationwide shortage of asylum spots means it takes time. “Although fewer people are registering for asylum in the Netherlands than before, the number of residents at our locations is increasing.” Some 80,000 people currently live in asylum centres.

COA attributes the problem to long asylum procedures and too few homes for people with a residence permit, meaning more people have to stay longer in shelters. “There are fewer new locations opening than there are closing,” it said.

The 300 asylum seekers in Balk, however, fulfil De Fryske Marren’s shelter obligations under the country’s distribution laws.

World.title: Ajax win at Sion, Twente lose at home in Conference League
World.content:
Ajax and FC Twente played the first legs of their Conference League play-off ties on Thursday evening, the last stage before the competition’s league phase. Ajax won 4-2 away at FC Sion in Switzerland, while Twente lost 1-0 at home to FK Qarabag.

Ajax fell behind to a goal just after 30 minutes but recovered after the break. Julian Brandt and Marcos Leonardo scored to put the visitors in front, before Sion equalised from the penalty spot through Ylyas Chouaref.

Tolu Arokodare headed in within a minute of coming on to restore the lead, and Davy Klaassen lobbed a fourth late on.

The match was shown in the Netherlands only on a €4.99 pay-per-view channel, a decision that had angered many fans in the build-up. Ajax will go through as long as they avoid losing by three or more goals in next Thursday’s return at the Johan Cruijff Arena.

Twente jeered at home

Twente had a good start in Enschede but faded, and Kady Borges scored shortly after half-time to hand Qarabag the lead. The home crowd began jeering the team, whistling at the players at full time and cheering the substitution of striker Wout Weghorst.

Qarabag, multiple-time Azerbaijani champions, reached the Champions League knockout stage last season. Both Dutch clubs had come through the previous qualifying round last week. Twente now face a difficult second leg in Baku next Thursday.

World.title: How will the Law and Justice split affect Polish politics?
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. By Aleks Szczerbiak The biggest-ever split within Poland’s main right-wing opposition party is a serious self-inflicted wound, signalling a more fragmented conservative landscape and complicating the right’s path back to power. While it provides a tactical boost for the Tusk government, there is still every chance of a conservative comeback if the right-wing parties cooperate effectively. Radical-right challengers At the end of last month, the right-wing Law and Justice (PiS) party, Poland’s ruling party between 2015 and 2023 and currently the main opposition grouping, saw the biggest split in its 25-year history. The rupture was the culmination of months of increasingly open and bitter factional conflict over the party’s future direction. PiS has for the last two decades been the dominant force on the Polish right. However, it lost power following the October 2023 parliamentary election, which led to the formation of a coalition headed up by Donald Tusk, leader of the liberal-centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party. Since last autumn, PiS has seen its polling numbers decline to the party’s lowest level of support for 15 years. At the same time, it has been challenged by two radical right competitors: the free-market Confederation (Konfederacja) and the ultra-nationalist Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), which together began to match, or even exceed, PiS’s level of support. Responding to declining support At the heart of this conflict was a bitter clash between longtime party leader Jarosław Kaczyński and Mateusz Morawiecki, who served as PiS prime minister from 2017 to 2023 but grew increasingly impatient with the former’s dominance. Two main factions emerged centred on a bitter dispute on how the party should respond to declining support and political competition on its right flank. The hardline traditionalist-conservative faction, often referred to as the “butter-makers” (maślarze), was more Eurosceptic and advocated a clearer right-wing agenda that included pushing ahead with radical state reconstruction and promoting a conservative vision of national identity and traditional values. In their reading, PiS lost support to its right-wing competitors because it was not radical enough and the solution was to sharpen its ideological profile and double down on hardline rhetoric. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 This group gained influence in party structures and when, in March, Kaczyński designated one of its key figures, former education minister Przemysław Czarnek, as the party’s prime ministerial candidate in the next parliamentary election, scheduled for autumn 2027, this was widely seen as a clear signal favouring the traditionalist-conservative faction. Morawiecki and his allies in the modernising-technocratic faction, often called the “scouts” (harcerze), also had strong conservative values and at times were very critical of Poland’s post-1989 establishment. However, they advocated a strategy of stressing economic competence, pragmatic governance and boosting Polish prosperity over hardline rhetoric on moral-cultural issues as a more effective way of appealing to voters less influenced by traditional institutions such as the Catholic church. Although they were also critical of Brussels overreach, Morawiecki’s faction preferred to avoid escalating conflict with the EU and argued that PiS had to broaden its appeal to younger, urban, more centrist-conservative Poles who found radical cultural rhetoric off-putting. Programmatic differences and personal ambitions The conflict became so destabilising because, although rooted in genuine programmatic and strategic disagreements, personalities and individual ambitions also played a major role. While Kaczyński maintained formal control of the party, his advancing age escalated debates over PiS’s direction and leadership, and these tensions intensified after the party failed to translate its presidential candidate Karol Nawrocki’s surprise summer 2025 election victory into broader momentum. For his part, Morawiecki grew increasingly impatient and frustrated as hardliners sidelined him, while his supporters were afraid that they would be excluded from PiS candidate lists at the next election. These long-simmering tensions came to a head in April, when Morawiecki announced the formation of Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), a think tank-like platform focused on economic development The association was widely interpreted by Kaczyński and PiS hardliners as a direct challenge to party unity and the leader’s authority. The leadership ruled that Development Plus violated the PiS statute, which explicitly prohibits members from joining political organisations that conflict with the party’s goals. While Morawiecki insisted that it was simply a modest intra-party policy forum, by registering an organisation with dozens of parliamentarians, he gave his faction a formal institutional shell that could potentially act as a launchpad for his own rival breakaway party. Initially, Kaczyński and Morawiecki came to a compromise agreement whereby Development Plus would work within an official party expert group. However, in July the situation escalated when the PiS leadership issued an ultimatum banning members from participating in internal political factions (clearly targeting Development Plus) and instructing parliamentarians to sign loyalty declarations confirming that they were not involved in any such groupings. Most complied, but 40 parliamentarians affiliated with Development Plus refused to do so, accusing the leadership of political blackmail. Ultimately, Kaczyński announced that, by refusing to sign, Morawiecki and his allies had effectively left the party, while Development Plus framed it as expulsion over policy differences caused by “plotters” surrounding the party leader. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 An even more fragmented right The loss of 40 deputies means that PiS is no longer the largest parliamentary caucus, thus losing procedural advantages, committee control and visibility. The departing group includes many experienced and talented politicians, particularly in the economic and foreign policy fields. The split also reduces PiS’s funding, staffing, and in some regions local organisation, as well as creating the risk of demoralisation and further defections. Even if the Polish right secures a parliamentary majority at the next election, PiS’s relative influence could be greatly reduced. Although Kaczyński’s formal party leadership remains unquestioned, the split signals to the broader right that his authority is waning and undermines his claim to be the undisputed hegemon and central broker on the right; he is increasingly now one leader among several. It also further erodes the model that Kaczyński has built over many years as the main ideologue and ultimate arbiter of internal PiS factions. In earlier crises, this personal authority and control gave him leverage to keep everyone on board so that disagreements were managed internally, and even disillusioned figures usually stayed in, or returned to, the party. Indeed, by adding a fourth distinctive player, the PiS split further compounds the divisions on the Polish right that have deepened since the last election, transforming what was once a relatively consolidated “big tent” bloc into a multi-polar competitive field. For sure, polls conducted after the split show the combined right-wing vote as competitive overall, but even if this level of support remains stable, or even increases slightly, it is now divided across more options. This is significant because Poland’s proportional electoral system uses the d’Hondt counting system that favours larger groupings. It also creates the risk that smaller right-wing parties such as Morawiecki’s new grouping could fall below the 5% parliamentary representation threshold, so their votes are excluded from seat allocation. All of this makes it harder for the right to translate raw voter support into political power. Moreover, even if the right-wing parties win a combined parliamentary majority, post-election coordination becomes much more complex with four (or more) actors whose leaders’ rivalries, different priorities and historical animosities complicate forming a stable coalition government. Nawrocki’s role will be crucial In the light of this, Nawrocki has emerged as a critical unifier with crossover appeal across the fractured Polish right. His presidential election victory showed that he could attract support well beyond traditional PiS loyalists and consolidate a broad right-wing coalition, including the vast majority of voters from both Confederations. As president, he operates outside direct party control and has cultivated an image as an authoritative unifying figure on the right, which gives him much greater moral and symbolic stature than a partisan leader immersed in day-to-day machinations. Nawrocki has also used his constitutional powers and standing, including a legislative veto that the government lacks the three-fifths parliamentary majority to overturn, to position himself assertively as a powerful counterweight to the Tusk administration, and is currently Poland’s most popular politician. Nonetheless, Nawrocki’s potential to act as a possible right-wing unifier and broker is limited. For sure, he can use the presidency to set a broad conservative agenda and mediate negotiations among the various right-wing groupings to secure pre- and post-election agreements. Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland's largest opposition party, PiS, has called on President @NawrockiKn to help unify the country’s various right-wing opposition forces ahead of next year’s parliamentary elections https://t.co/Q3BFSOSfTG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 10, 2026 However, Nawrocki has no formal unifying mandate and his success ultimately depends on whether the various actors are willing to be led. Without broader cooperation, even his efforts will only mitigate, not eliminate, the damage from a divided right, and personal and ideological rivalries currently run deep and cannot be easily overridden. Moreover, not only is the president expected to remain formally above the fray and not engage too openly in day-to-day politics, he also lacks the control over party organisational machinery needed to micro-manage and enforce messy backroom deals. Pivotal but not transformative? Initial polling conducted since the split suggests that Morawiecki’s new grouping would likely clear the 5% threshold and enter parliament with a small-to-medium-sized fraction; according to Politico Europe, it is currently averaging around 6% support. Although this could make it a pivotal player in coalition talks, it does not suggest that the grouping can dramatically reshape the country’s political landscape. Moreover, its support appears to be drawn mainly from PiS’s traditional electoral base, so it is simply further fragmenting the existing right-wing vote rather than drawing in a significant number of new voters who hitherto supported the governing coalition parties. For sure, Morawiecki‘s project has advantages that many newcomers lack, notably its leader’s very high name recognition and a sizeable bloc of high-profile, political heavyweight allies, much larger than any previous PiS breakaway faction. His grouping immediately became the third largest parliamentary fraction, giving it visibility, funding, and organisational backbone. However, although there are some rare exceptions that usually involve major figures with significant resources breaking from established parties, it is a familiar pattern in post-1989 Polish politics for a brand new “startup” party to show an early bounce, benefiting from initial media coverage, only to fade or disappear as voters drift back to more established groupings or abstain at the next election. Sustaining momentum requires local organisational infrastructure, reliable funding, rapid professionalisation, and a clear identity, which new parties often lack. Indeed, to be successful a new startup should really attract at least 10% support initially simply because of its “newness”. Over the years, PiS breakaway politicians have established new parties that either quickly disappeared from the political scene or were eventually reintegrated into the grouping. Temporary relief for Tusk From a short-term tactical perspective, the PiS split is a welcome political gift for the Tusk government, shifting the media focus away from criticisms of its record and recent scandals and controversies. It has for example, blunted the opposition’s ability to maintain a sustained assault over a scandal involving high earnings for, and mismanagement by, a KO-connected doctor, alleged VIP access and potential patient harm at the Warsaw South Hospital, which had previously dominated the summer news headlines. The ruling coalition is likely to survive until next year's election, but its prospects are hampered by a weak domestic record, writes @AleksSzczerbiak The government has therefore made security key to its reelection narrative, but that also carries risks https://t.co/w2UeNaTwAO — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 1, 2026 However, the PiS split has not resolved the deeper image and performance problems that have dragged down the Tusk government’s approval ratings. The administration struggles with perceptions of slow delivery on promises while facing a hostile president, and if these problems persist, or new controversies reignite strongly once the PiS drama cools, the government will very quickly find itself back on the defensive. The PiS split only provides temporary relief; to win the next election, the ruling coalition needs to improve its own standing, not rely on opposition mistakes. World.title: Polish NGOs urge PM’s “right-hand man” to withdraw constitutional court candidacy
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
